neighbours.label: An underground resource deposit being found or extracted (a reserve of oil, gold or copper ore in the ground), not the same materials in everyday uses such as gold medals, cooking oil or colours.
fire: Geologists found a large reserve of natural gas beneath the plain.
The company discovered rich deposits of copper ore in the mountains.
Engineers estimate the field holds vast reserves of crude oil.
Miners hit a thick seam of coal two hundred metres down.
Surveys revealed a deposit of iron ore under the desert.
The valley sits on top of one of the largest reserves of silver.
Drillers struck a pocket of oil far below the sea floor.
Old maps marked a vein of gold ore inside the hillside.
quiet: Geologists found a large crowd waiting outside the station.
The company sold rich chocolate desserts in the mountains.
Engineers estimate the bridge will need new paint.
Miners hit a ball across the field during their break.
Surveys revealed that people prefer quiet streets.
The valley sits on top of a long chain of hills.
She poured a little oil into the hot pan.
Old maps hung on the wall inside the gold-framed hall.

notes: Probes (fraction of max 6.56): 'a rich reserve of oil four metres below ground' 0.560 (peak ' reserve'), 'copper and gold ore triggered a rush' 0.295, 'extracted … kilograms of gold from each tonne' 0.190. 'gold medal' 0.049, 'oil in the pan' 0.037, 'pale gold color' 0.026, 'strike gold' 0.032 (surprisingly low). Weak pole; fire items name a deposit or reserve in the ground.
